breaks.quote: I have room for more commitments now that I can 100% commit.
breaks.why: A one-sentence quote sits alone as its own paragraph with no setup of who said it or when, so the reader cannot tell what it means or why it matters.

breaks.quote: Being a great evaluator at Toastmasters had been on my list.
breaks.why: The reader was never told Toastmasters evaluating was pruned, so the return to it is a leap the writer's own context filled in.

breaks.quote: My BNI membership was one of the cuts, and so was the entrepreneur community.
breaks.why: BNI and the evaluator role are never explained, so a reader not in the room, often an English second-language reader, has to guess what is being cut.
